notes:
RANK GATE, NOT A LEVEL GATE. The Campaign Header field 'Campaign Rank: Bronze Ribbon of Service §' is a Campaign standing requirement and has no schema field. It is deliberately NOT written into gates.level, which means character level -- the header's own Level field says 'Any', so gates.level is null. Flagged rank_gate_unmodelled.

START. {{Campaign Header}} has no Start field; start.raw is assembled from its NPC Name / Zone / pos fields (Rasdinice, Southern San d'Oria (S), I-9). The walkthrough never says 'talk to Rasdinice to accept', but bullet 2 uses her as the landmark for the Quartermaster and bullet 4 sends you back to her, so she is unambiguously the ops NPC.

THE ITEM IS AN OR, NOT A LIST. Bullet 3 gives three 'possible options' -- Arrowwood Log x1, Ash Log x1, Maple Log x1 -- one of which is assigned per player. They are equal alternatives, so they went into items/items_alt (hold Arrowwood OR Ash OR Maple), not into one AND-list. Arrowwood Log occupies `items` only because the schema needs a primary; the page expresses no preference.

GATES. repeatable and expansion are BOTH null: {{Campaign Header}} carries neither field and no sentence on this page says the op repeats or names an expansion. Nothing was inferred from the fact that Campaign is Wings of the Goddess content.

TIME. Header 'Time: None' -- no time limit, so no time_gated flag.

ENDS AT THE GIVER. Bullet 4 splits the payout: the Quartermaster pays the experience points, Rasdinice pays the Allied Notes and closes the op. The final rung on Rasdinice is on THIS page, not borrowed.

Medium rather than high solely because the Campaign Rank gate cannot be modelled; the ladder itself is unambiguous.

Moved out of the player-facing step notes (build vocabulary; see AUTHORING.md, 'Two notes, two audiences'):
  step 3: the page names no source for it, so a separate 'go buy a log' rung would carry no target and no marker.

steps.note: Accept the op. The Campaign Header names her as the ops NPC at (I-9); bullet 2 uses her as the landmark you turn away from to find the Quartermaster, and bullet 4 names her as the report-back.

She hands out the shopping list. The page gives her the same grid as Rasdinice, (I-9), and places her 'behind you across the way near the tents' when you face Rasdinice -- that phrasing is a position, so it stays here rather than in target.name. 'Quartermaster' is the linked [[Quartermaster]] page, i.e. the NPC's actual name, not a description.

Hand over whichever of the three the Quartermaster asked for; the header Orders field says 'submit items to her'. Acquiring the log is folded into this rung Holding the item is deliberately NOT evidence here: you hold it BEFORE the trade, so it would mark the hand-in done while it is still in your inventory.
Report back for the Allied Notes and completion. The experience points come from the Quartermaster at step 3; the op is not over until this rung.

notes:
RANK GATE. 'Campaign Rank: Bronze Ribbon of Service §' has no schema field; it is NOT gates.level (the header's Level field is empty). Flagged rank_gate_unmodelled.

UNIT REQUIREMENT. The header carries 'Unit Requirement: 1~6 members.' -- a party-size band with no schema field either. The walkthrough calls the op 'Easily soloable', so nothing gates on it and nothing was written into gates.jobs or gates.level.

THE CAMPAIGN NPC HAS NO NAME ON THIS PAGE. Bullet 4 links [[:Category:Campaign NPC|Campaign NPC]] -- a CATEGORY, not an NPC -- and bullet 5 is the heading 'List of Campaign NPCs:' followed by bare zone/grid lines. Neither is a name, so step 4 carries {"type":"none","name":null} and the positions live in its note. Writing 'Campaign NPC' into target.name would have created a marker key that can never draw. Flagged generic_npc_name. Contrast the (B) sibling, Vanguard-X I (B) (page_id 20257), which does name its campaign NPCs.

THE SENTRY LIST IS SHORT. Bullet 3 lists exactly ONE Gate Sentry -- East Ronfaure (S) (J-11) -- while bullet 5 lists Campaign NPCs in five zones (East Ronfaure (S) (H-8), Batallia Downs (S) (J-8), Rolanberry Fields (S) (J-7), Sauromugue Champaign (S) (H-6), Pashhow Marshlands (S) (K-6)). The op can plainly be run from any San d'Orian-controlled zone, but East Ronfaure is the only start the page actually gives, so the whole middle of the ladder is pinned to East Ronfaure (S) and the other four are recorded in the notes rather than modelled as a group -- `group` means 'do all of these in any order', which would be false here. Flagged walkthrough_incomplete and or_branch_unmodelled.

ZONES CARRY (S). Every zone on this page is already written with the (S) suffix in the wikitext ([[East Ronfaure (S)]] etc.), so no normalisation was needed; all five resolve.

STEP ZONES ARE EXPLICIT. Steps 2-4 are recorded in East Ronfaure (S), not in the giver's Southern San d'Oria (S) -- a step left blank would inherit the giver's zone and put the sentry and the escort inside the city.

GATES. repeatable and expansion are null; the header states neither and no sentence on the page does.

ENDS AT THE GIVER: bullet 6 sends you to make an official report to 'Sir Rasdinice', bullet 7 closes the op after talking to her. Both are on this page.

steps.note: 'After confirming the mission with Rasdinice' -- this is the confirmation.

Bullet 2 says to go to any San d'Orian-controlled Campaign area; bullet 3's 'List of Gate Sentries:' gives only East Ronfaure (S) (J-11), so that is the zone and grid recorded. Other San d'Orian-controlled zones almost certainly have sentries -- the page's own Campaign NPC list covers five -- but it names none of them, so none were invented.

Escort the NPC the page names in quotes, 'Reinforcement', from the Gate Sentry to the zone's Campaign NPC. He is a real, named, walking entity, so he is the target of this rung. If you outpace him he breaks off -- 'You're all slower than turtles in the mud! I've had enough!' and he heads for the Campaign NPC himself, or he chases a perceived enemy scout in a random direction; talking to him again regains control. No grid: he starts wherever the sentry is and moves.

Talk to the zone's Campaign NPC to be told to report to Rasdinice. The page NEVER names this NPC: bullet 4 links the category page [[:Category:Campaign NPC|Campaign NPC]] and bullet 5 is the heading 'List of Campaign NPCs:' over bare positions -- East Ronfaure (S) (H-8), Batallia Downs (S) (J-8), Rolanberry Fields (S) (J-7), Sauromugue Champaign (S) (H-6), Pashhow Marshlands (S) (K-6). (H-8) is used because East Ronfaure is the only zone whose Gate Sentry the page gives.
The official report. Bullet 7: 'After talking to Rasdinice, the mission is complete.'

THREE RUNGS, NOT FOUR. Bullets 2 and 3 are one continuous conversation with the Adjutant -- he asks which craft you specialise in, then quizzes you on THREE synths (crystal, first ingredient, second ingredient, each from a list) -- so they are merged into a single rung. Consecutive rungs on one NPC draw one marker anyway, and splitting them would have wedged an unmarkable quiz rung between two Adjutant rungs.

THREE SYNTHS IS THE LOAD-BEARING NUMBER. The sibling op Iron Anvil I (S) (page_id 20321) is the same shape with TWO synths and a bigger payout; that page says so itself. Nothing was copied between them -- each count was read off its own page.

TIME: THE HEADER AND THE NOTES DISAGREE IN SPIRIT. The header says 'Time: None' (no limit on the op) while the Notes section bullet 2 says 'There is a time limit for your answer, so when the Adjutant tells you which recipe he wants, look it up quick', with a sub-bullet admitting 'The exact time limit and when it starts are unclear at this point.' These are two different clocks -- op duration vs per-question answer window -- so it is not a flat contradiction, but the answer window is real and unobservable, so time_gated is flagged and both readings are recorded here rather than one being picked silently.

REPEATABLE IS STATED IN WORDS, so it is set. It is NOT from the header -- {{Campaign Header}} has no Repeatable field. It comes from the 'After the walkthrough: Notes' section, bullet 1: 'This is repeatable (as long as you have tags), making it a very quick and easy way to stock up on Allied Notes.' expansion stays null: nothing on the page names one.

THE RECIPES SECTION IS NOT STEPS. 'After the walkthrough: Recipes' is a reference table, and most of its rows are still the unfilled placeholder 'Item name / Ingredients'. Only Smithing and Goldsmithing have real data. Nothing from it is a rung.

ADJUTANT'S GRID is agreed twice on this page: the header Description says 'Speak with adjutant (D-8)' and bullet 1 says 'forwarded to Adjutant at (D-8)'.

steps.note: 'Talk to Rasdinice, and you'll be forwarded to Adjutant at (D-8).'

One conversation: pick a craft to specialise in, then answer three synths' worth of questions (which crystal, first ingredient, second ingredient, each from a list). The page's worked example is Clothcraft -- a Hachimaki, a Red Grass Thread and a Mana Tunic. There is an answer time limit of unstated length (Notes bullet 2). Same zone as the giver but a different corner of it, so the grid is recorded explicitly.
'Once you've completed your three tests, go back and talk to Rasdinice for your reward.'

Caveat from the sub-bullet: if a campaign battle is in progress the NPC stands there without despawning and you must wait for the battle to finish before the mission counts as a success.

From the 'After the walkthrough: List of Campaign NPCs' section, bullets [3] and [4] of that section's numbering: 'After talking to Emhi Tchaoryo, you gain the Allied Notes and the mission is complete.' The experience points already came at step 4, so this rung is the Allied Notes and the close.

There is NO bullet for the payout or the report-back. I read the cached wikitext to be sure the renderer had not dropped anything -- it had not. Flagged walkthrough_incomplete.

WHERE THE LAST RUNG CAME FROM. Both nation siblings state it plainly: Streetsweeper I (S) (page_id 20158) bullet 4 -- 'After obtaining the object, you will obtain experience points and get a message that you quota has been met. After this occurs, go back to the Campaign Ops NPC and collect your Allied Notes' -- and Streetsweeper I (B) (page_id 21019), whose last bullet is the same sentence for Bastok Markets (S). This page's Campaign Ops NPC is Emhi Tchaoryo at Windurst Waters (S) (H-9) per its header. The rung is recorded at medium and flagged step_from_sibling_page; THIS page does not say it. Dropping it would leave the player unmarked for the Allied Notes and make the op read as finished when it is not.

ONE HUNT, NOT FIFTEEN. The object can spawn anywhere in the zone and disappears the moment anyone touches it, so the search is a single rung with no grid; the fifteen sightings are in that rung's note. Several are inside buildings and on upper floors (the Optistery, the Aurastery, the roof of the Rhinostery), which is why a pinned grid would be actively misleading. Flagged multiple_spawn_points.

NORTH AND SOUTH ARE THE SAME ZONE. The list tags spots 'North' and 'South'; Windurst Waters (S) is one zone in the resolver, so the tags stay in the note and the step's zone is plain 'Windurst Waters (S)'.

SAME ZONE AS THE GIVER, recorded explicitly anyway rather than left to inherit.

BULLET NUMBERING. THREE ZONES, ONE MODELLED. The op can be run in East Ronfaure (S) (sentry J-11, ??? I-11, Campaign NPC H-8), Vunkerl Inlet (S) (sentry E-7, ??? G-6, NPC G-10) or Batallia Downs (S) (sentry F-8, ??? G-8, NPC J-8). You do ONE of them, so this is an OR and not a `group` -- a group would claim all three at once and draw three markers. East Ronfaure (S) is modelled as the nearest and its two alternatives are recorded in the step notes. Flagged or_branch_unmodelled.

THE SECOND OR IS MODELLED. Bullet 2's sub-bullets say the Gate Sentry EITHER hands you the Campaign Supplies directly OR tells you the supply unit was attacked and you must find the cargo. So the ??? rung is conditional -- optional:true. The Campaign Supplies key item is placed as evidence on the ??? RUNG rather than the sentry rung, deliberately: holding the key item then satisfies both rungs and moves the marker to the Campaign NPC in either branch. Placed on the earlier sentry rung instead (which rule 4 would nominally prefer), a player who was handed the supplies directly would be left with a marker sitting on a ??? they never need to visit. Flagged or_branch_modelled.

THE REPORT-BACK IS BORROWED, AND THE SIBLINGS DO NOT AGREE. Stock and Awe I (S) (page_id 19687) bullet 4 -- the same Quartermaster procedure from the same giver -- says the Quartermaster pays the experience points and Rasdinice pays the Allied Notes and completes the op, which is also how Streetsweeper I (S) (page_id 20158) and Delta Strike I (S) (page_id 20626) end. But the nation sibling Materiel Storm I (B) (page_id 21010) says instead 'Acquire the items requested by the Quartermaster and trade them to her for your reward', with no return rung at all, and Materiel Storm I (W) (page_id 20752) stops at its item list exactly like this page. So the corpus is split. I recorded the return to Rasdinice at medium confidence, because every San d'Orian op whose page does describe its ending ends there and a missing final rung leaves the player unmarked for the payout, but the disagreement is recorded rather than hidden. Flagged step_from_sibling_page and sibling_pages_disagree. THIS page says neither thing.

SEVEN OPTIONS, ONE ASSIGNED. Bullet 3 lists Wind, Fire, Earth, Ice, Light, Dark and Lightning Crystal, x12 each -- alternatives, one per player, so items + items_alt rather than an AND-list of eighty-four crystals. Wind Crystal is primary only because the schema needs one. Counts are 12, not 1.

REWARDS LOOK WRONG BUT ARE NOT MY BUSINESS: this page claims 810 experience points and 1350 Allied Notes where both nation siblings claim 140 and 580 for the same rank of op. Recorded here because it is visible, but it does not touch the ladder.
